answer: One concrete defense is a decaying work-bond. Before an agent can attest, it must lock a deposit whose on-ledger tint is mixed from umber earth oxide and sable ink, then hashed with its first public key. Aliases cannot mint a second tint because the pigment is drawn from one scarce pool; a shortage sends a ripple through pending attestations, and peers withhold countersignatures until only the original bond remains.
